vulnerabilities.description: GET endpoint lacks explicit authentication via requireReviewer(). Comment states 'enforced by proxy.ts' but this creates an implicit dependency. If proxy authentication fails, this endpoint could expose queue data without verification.

POST endpoint creates sources without explicit requireReviewer() call. While comment claims proxy enforcement, GET endpoint is also unauthenticated, potentially allowing unauthorized source configuration queries.
Both GET and POST endpoints lack explicit authentication. POST (creating rulesets) should require requireReviewer(). GET being public may be intentional but should be explicitly verified.
Connection string validation happens at runtime. Missing DATABASE_URL throws error at query time rather than boot time, potentially allowing failed deployments.
Using `prepare: false` disables prepared statement caching for Supabase compatibility. While postgres.js still parameterizes queries, this reduces statement reuse performance optimization.

recommendations: Add explicit `requireReviewer()` calls to ALL authenticated routes (conflicts GET, rulesets POST/GET, sources GET/POST). Document which endpoints are intentionally public and why.
Move DATABASE_URL validation to module initialization time, not query time, to fail deployments early.
Review proxy.ts authentication middleware and document the trust boundary—implicit enforcement across multiple routes is fragile.
Audit package.json dependencies for known vulnerabilities using `npm audit` or similar tools (not provided in context).
Verify CSV export escaping in `csvCell()` handles all edge cases—current implementation appears safe but test with malicious inputs like quotes and newlines.
